questions.question: Which field is added to tables to enable domain separation?

explanation.correct: By default, domain separation adds a sys_domain field to the Task [task] and Configuration Items [cmdb_ci] tables and their extensions. This field stores the domain to which each record belongs.

wrongAnswers.explanation: sys_tenant is not a standard domain separation field
The correct field name is sys_domain, not domain_id
sys_scope is used for application scoping, not domain separation

source.excerpt: By default, domain separation adds a domain field to the Task [task] and Configuration Items [cmdb_ci] tables and their extensions.

questions.question: In a domain hierarchy, a user in a parent domain can view records from which domains by default?

options.text: Their domain, child domains, and domains they have visibility into

explanation.correct: From a domain, users can see records in the global domain, their specific domain, any child domain of that domain, or any domain that gets directly or indirectly contained by that domain. This follows the platform's visibility domains and contains domains rules.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Users in parent domains can see child domain records by default, not just their own domain
Users cannot see all domains by default; visibility is limited by domain hierarchy and explicit visibility grants
While global domain records are visible, users also see their own domain and child domains

source.excerpt: From that domain you can see CIs in global domain, the specific domain, any child domain of that domain or any domain that gets directly or indirectly contained by that domain.

questions.question: Which statement accurately describes what happens when records are automatically generated in a domain-separated environment?

options.text: Records are always created in the global domain
The domain of the record is the same as the domain of the user creating or generating the records
Records are randomly assigned to available domains
Records inherit the domain of the parent table

explanation.correct: For records that are automatically generated (and for any record that is manually generated), the domain of the record is the same as the domain of the user responsible for creating or generating the records. This is critical for ensuring records are visible to the right set of users.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Records are not always created in the global domain; they inherit the creating user's domain
Domain assignment is deterministic based on the user's domain, not random
Records inherit the user's domain, not the parent table's domain configuration

source.excerpt: For records that are automatically generated (and for any GRC record that is manually generated), the domain of the record is the same as the domain of the user responsible for creating or generating the records.

questions.question: Which is NOT a recommended practice when domain separating tables?

options.text: Adding sys_domain field to custom tables
Domain separating platform tables with sys_ prefix
Using the CI Class Manager for CMDB domain configuration

explanation.correct: ServiceNow does not recommend domain separating platform tables (any table with the sys_ prefix such as the Dictionary Entry [sys_dictionary] and Dictionary Entry Override [sys_dictionary_override] tables) because it can produce unexpected results.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Adding sys_domain field to custom tables is the recommended way to enable domain separation for those tables
Creating domain-specific business rules is a valid approach for process separation
CI Class Manager is the recommended tool for managing CMDB domain configurations

source.excerpt: Warning: ServiceNow does not recommend domain separating platform tables (any table with the sys_ prefix such as the Dictionary Entry [sys_dictionary] and Dictionary Entry Override [sys_dictionary_override] tables) because it can produce unexpected results.

questions.question: Which tables have the sys_domain field added by default when domain separation is enabled? (Choose two)

explanation.correct: By default, domain separation adds a domain field to the Task [task] and Configuration Items [cmdb_ci] tables and their extensions. These are the primary data tables that typically need domain separation for multi-tenant implementations.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Dictionary Entry is a system table (sys_ prefix) that should not be domain separated
System Properties is a platform configuration table, not domain separated by default
Script Include is a development artifact table, handled differently than data tables

source.excerpt: By default, domain separation adds a domain field to the Task [task] and Configuration Items [cmdb_ci] tables and their extensions.

questions.question:
Evaluate the following statements about domain visibility:

Statement 1: Users always have access to data from domains that have been explicitly granted to them by domain visibility.

Statement 2: A user in a child domain can always view records in the parent domain.

Which statements are TRUE?

explanation.correct: Statement 1 is TRUE: Users always have access to data from domains that have been explicitly granted to them by domain visibility. Statement 2 is FALSE: An incident in the parent domain can reference artifacts in the child domain, but not the other way around. Child domains cannot automatically access parent domain records.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Statement 1 is true about explicit domain visibility grants; Statement 2 is false because child domains don't automatically see parent records
Statement 2 is false; child domains cannot view parent domain records by default
Statement 1 is true regarding explicit domain visibility grants

source.excerpt: The overarching principles of visibility in separated domains in the NOW Platform apply. As always, an incident in the parent domain can reference artifacts in the child domain, but not the other way around.

questions.question: A service provider has domains organized as: Global > TOP > Domain A and Domain B. If a control needs to be assessed by users in both Domain A and Domain B, where should the control be created?

explanation.correct: If you have a risk or control that you want to be assessed by users in domains A and B, the risk or control should be generated or manually created at the global level. If the control is created in Domain B, you will not be able to recreate it in Domain A due to indexing constraints.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Creating in Domain A only would make it inaccessible to Domain B users
Creating in Domain B only would make it inaccessible to Domain A users
Creating at TOP would work for users in TOP and child domains, but global is more appropriate when both sibling domains need access

source.excerpt: If you have a risk or control that you want to be assessed by users in domains A and B, the risk or control should be generated or manually created at the global level.

questions.question: What happens to security incidents in a domain-separated Security Incident Response implementation?

options.text: All security incidents are visible across all domains
Security incidents in one domain cannot be viewed from other domains
Security incidents are automatically shared with parent domains
Security incidents must be manually assigned to each domain

explanation.correct: Data can be domain-separated, which means security incidents in one domain can't be viewed from other domains. Observables extracted from the security incident are placed in the same domain and can't be viewed from other domains.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Domain separation specifically prevents cross-domain visibility of security incidents
Child domain incidents are not automatically shared with parent domains in the way described
Domain assignment is automatic based on the creating user's domain, not manual

source.excerpt: Security incidents in one domain can't be viewed from other domains. Observables extracted from the security incident are placed in the same domain and can't be viewed from other domains.

questions.question: Which aspects of domain separation are included when the application supports domain separation at runtime? (Choose three)

explanation.correct: At the Basic support level, the application supports domain separation at run time including: separation from the user interface, cache keys, reporting, rollups, and aggregations. These are the fundamental runtime aspects of domain separation.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Automatic data backup is not part of domain separation functionality
Database table partitioning is a database administration feature, not a domain separation feature

source.excerpt: The application supports domain separation at run time. The domain separation includes separation from the user interface, cache keys, reporting, rollups, and aggregations.

questions.question:
Evaluate the following statements about IRE (Identification and Reconciliation Engine) domain separation modes:

Statement 1: In Strict mode, identification processes only those CIs where the domain ID is identical to the domain of the currently logged-in user.

Statement 2: In Platform domain separation mode, duplicate CIs across different domains are NOT considered duplicates by IRE.

Which statements are TRUE?

explanation.correct: Statement 1 is TRUE: In Strict mode (enabled by default), identification processes only those CIs in which the domain ID is identical to the domain of the currently logged-in user. Statement 2 is FALSE: When Platform domain separation mode is enabled, duplicate CIs that exist across domains (such as parent and child domains) ARE considered as duplicate CIs by IRE.

wrongAnswers.explanation: Statement 2 is false; Platform mode considers cross-domain duplicates as duplicates. Statement 1 is true about Strict mode.
Statement 2 is false; Platform mode considers cross-domain CIs as potential duplicates
Statement 1 is true about Strict mode behavior

source.excerpt: Strict mode (enabled by default): In this mode, identification processes only those CIs in which the domain ID is identical to the domain of the currently logged in user. When platform domain separation mode is enabled, Duplicate CIs that exist across domains are considered as duplicate CIs by IRE.

questions.question: What should a user do to extend domain separation to a new custom table they have created?

options.text: Add a sys_domain field to the table's dictionary definition
Enable the table in Domain Support plugin settings

explanation.correct: You can extend domain separation to any new tables you create by adding a sys_domain field to the table's dictionary definition. By default, the system only domain-separates platform and baseline application tables where appropriate.

wrongAnswers.explanation: ACLs control access permissions but do not enable domain separation; the sys_domain field is required
Domain visibility records control user access to domains, not table-level domain separation
There is no specific plugin setting to enable tables; you must add the sys_domain field to the table

source.excerpt: You can extend domain separation to any new tables you create by adding a sys_domain field to the table's dictionary definition.
